geographic_notes.text: Source dated 2023-11 reports: Bangkok, Nakhon Ratchasima and Ubon Ratchathani recur among the top-ten modeled heat, drought and flood risk areas for water management under both RCP lists.
Source dated 2023-11 reports: For agriculture, Nakhon Ratchasima, Khon Kaen and Ubon Ratchathani appear in both modeled RCP top-ten lists for drought risk.
Source dated 2023-11 reports: Bangkok and Nakhon Ratchasima occur in both modeled flood-risk top-ten lists for the NAP's human-settlements-and-security sector.
Source dated 2025 reports: The report describes recurring drought and floods in Khon Kaen; 2021 floods averaged three months, while water insecurity deepened poverty among low-income agriculturists.

Source dated 2025 reports: Khon Kaen's water subcommittee convened 14 agencies and local stakeholders; risk mapping and consultation informed an integrated plan and a five-municipality urban-flood project.

A 2025 document-analysis chapter recounts a cited 2004 Songkhla drought case: anticipated rice losses prompted stockpiling, and an existing insurgent group raided fields to control food resources, with villagers reportedly killed. This is a secondary historical account, not independently verified causal identification; the reported percentage increase is omitted.

Source dated 2026-04-02 reports: In Yupo Subdistrict, Yala, women describe irregular rain, long droughts and severe floods disrupting rubber-tapping and small-farm livelihoods and raising crop-pumping fuel costs.
Source dated 2026-04-02 reports: The story caption reports floodwaters over 2.5 metres in Yupo on 25 November 2025, leaving approximately 300 families stranded.

Source dated 2026-04-02 reports: Yupo networks share early warnings, food and supplies; during the November 2025 flood, a mosque sheltered 50 residents and a community kitchen served about 300 families.

known_gaps.text: Automated machine-screening is not independent source verification. Routine/default app-use approval does not certify claims or sources. 14 of 14 evidence records and 1 of 1 pathways lack claim-level verification in this remediation; review the linked records before relying on them.
No existing THA country baseline was present in EXISTING_COUNTRIES.json.
Thailand's 2026 Taylor & Francis climate-conflict article was not used: direct publisher access returned 403, so indexed text remains leads-only.
The Fourth National Communication timed out and the Fourth Biennial Update Report exceeded retrieval limits; no claims rely on their indexed excerpts.
The Save the Children PDF was inaccessible; its findings are limited to the official resource-page abstract, which does not provide sample details or province-level results.
The 2004 Songkhla drought-conflict pathway is a secondary-cited historical account in a 2025 document-analysis chapter, not independent causal identification.
No inspected primary source documented conflict or insecurity directly blocking climate-adaptation implementation or services; this remains a search gap.

The Songkhla account is secondary-cited historical evidence, not independent identification of a climate effect. The numerical killing increase was omitted because underlying incident records were not independently checked.
The chapter's undated general conflict projection was excluded. No migration or ethnic-group threat inference is supported.
Southern-border gender findings are limited to the publisher's abstract; sample, full methods and local causal mechanisms were inaccessible.
No verified reverse-FCV blockage of adaptation was found. Yupo community accounts and response outputs are not representative impact evaluations.
Routine/default app-use approval granted by Lindsey Jones on 2026-10-27; independent source verification remains incomplete. Lending eligibility is not an FCV classification.
